summary: This Docker Compose configuration sets up a Python development container named app_python. It builds from a Dockerfile in the current directory using the 'development' stage, passes in several customizable environment variables for Python version and container user settings, and mounts the local codebase plus two named volumes to persist VSCode extensions and bash history across container restarts.

explanations.7: The 'target: development' tells Docker to build only up to the 'development' stage in the Dockerfile, stopping before any production-only layers—this keeps the development image leaner.
explanations.10: This passes the DOCKER_PYTHON_VERSION environment variable to the Dockerfile's build process so it knows which Python version to install; if not set, the build will fail unless the Dockerfile has a default.
explanations.12: The syntax ${DOCKER_APP_HOME:-/app} means 'use the DOCKER_APP_HOME variable if it exists, otherwise default to /app'—the colon-dash is a fallback operator.
explanations.21: The user field sets which user account runs processes inside the container; it's formatted as userid:groupid (like 1000:1000), and defaults to 1000 if those variables aren't defined.
explanations.27: This mounts the current directory (.) from your computer into the container at the path stored in DOCKER_APP_HOME, so code changes on your machine are immediately visible inside the container.
explanations.29: This creates a persistent volume that survives container restarts, storing VSCode's extensions so you don't have to reinstall them every time you restart the container.
explanations.31: Similarly, this volume stores bash command history, so your terminal history persists between container sessions.
